newsitem.title: JAPAN: Namco to open six game centres in Europe, Israel.
newsitem.headline: Namco to open six game centres in Europe, Israel.

text.p: Commercial game equipment maker and game centre operator Namco Ltd said on Tuesday it would open a total of six game centres in France, Germany, Britain and Israel by mid-1997.
It also wants to increase the number of its game centres in France, Britain, Germany and Spain to 25 in three years from nine currently, a company spokeswoman said.
It wants to boost its combined sales in the four countries to six billion yen a year in three years, further increasing to 10 billion yen a year in five years, the spokeswoman said.
The spokeswoman could not immediately provide Namco's current sales in the four countries.

She said Namco had set up a wholly owned unit in France in June this year and was already operating six game centres there. It was planning to open another centre in November, investing 150 million yen.
Namco also plans to form a wholly owned subsidiary in Germany and to open a game centre there in September, investing about 350 million yen, she said.
Namco also plans to open three more game centres in Britian by summer 1997, she said. The total investment for the three new outlets would be 1.3 billion yen.
Besides six outlets in France, Namco now operates two game centres in Britain and one in Spain, she said.
In Israel, Namco plans to set up a joint venture with an Israeli partner and open a game centre in September, investing about 400 million yen.
